begin: ^Oh? Finally, you're awake. I almost feel bad interrupting your sound sleep.

g-0: ^Shhh. Questions are for later. All I can say is that you’re in a place where you should be.
^It doesn't matter, not as much as who you are...
g-1: ^Don't worry. It's supposed to be that way.
g-2: ^Tch, questions again. Impatient, aren't we? Being you, that's how it should be.
^It takes a while to explain, but for now, just know that you're the protagonist of this story.
g-3: ^A hero. A leading character in a tale. Lord, you don't have stories where you come from?
^Stories...then I guess you too are a character of some kind?
^Can you tell me who you are at least?
g-4: ^Mhmm... I can only tell you that I'm a kind of divinity.

c-9: ^You can, but I can see you're the type that won't waste your time fighting a losing battle. We're fine, then.
c-10: ^I hope this little trick is enough to convince you.

c-11: ^Then let’s continue. Shall we go along and humor each other a bit?
c-12: ^I've done my part, if it can't convince you, let the rest of the world do it. Shall we play along and humor each other a bit?

quiz1: ^What alias do you want to be called by? We're starting fresh, after all.
^Then... let me tell you a story. One that I think you may find familiar.
^There was this princess, hair of the ebony, skin of snow, and the smiles on her lips bloom as red as the loveliest of roses. She's known as, you may have guessed, the fairest of them all.
^Almost everyone treasured her. Almost, aside from the Queen, her stepmother. Who was also a great mage. Who wanted to be the "fairest of them all" above everything.
^And so, the Queen wanted the princess dead. For such a reason. Petty, I daresay?
^Royals are never so simple. There must be something else.

c-0: ^Someone that petty coming to such a great power. My, my, you're as naive as I thought.
^But it's just a minor detail. Let's go on.
c-1: ^But that's just a minor detail, let's continue.
g-0: ^In response to that, what do you think the girl should do?
^Expose the Queen intention to her father.

c-2: ^A very straightforward approach. I like your spirits.
^But what could a small girl do against the all-powerful queen, doused to the teeth with magical prowess?
c-3: ^Really, depending on the King? How do you think the queen get so powerful? Her Father was a good parent, wasn't that much of a ruler.
c-4: ^...Seems like a wise choice. I wish life would be so easy.
c-5: ^A realistic approach. A little girl raised in wealth and admiration, now alone in the place where life's boiled down to mere survival.

g-1: ^But, what do you think the girl chose?
g-2: ^...She chose all of them. She ran off to the wood with her face changed. Not with the naive mind of merely to survive, but rather the strong will to stay safe until she gathered enough power for a back strike.

^This is where the dwarves come into play. They are hunted by the queendom for certain reasons. The girl ran into them during her escape. And they somehow managed to live together. What a fate, I daresay?
^What did the princess do to fit in? Your take?
^What she needed to do in that situation. You know?

c-11: ^Yes. How else would she survive? With now the whole queendom on her tail. But you shouldn't just fight the ones who are now your housemates.
c-12: ^The obvious choice. If only it were that simple. This isn't a tale where a song can save you and mere chores can keep your head on your neck.
c-13: ^Dirty-minded, aren't you?... But you're not entirely wrong either.

g-3: ^Well, you might have guessed the answer by now. Again, she did all of them. There wasn't any other way.
^There were more things like the poison apple or the mad prince that I'd love to continue on. But our time is up. So this will be our final question.
^...If you had the power to change fates, would you help the girl?
g-4: ^I feel my eyelids heavy and the sleep's about to take over me.
^I may have known what I need to know about you, and I can only wish you the best. It’s about time for your journey to start.
^Be rested and aware, for the paths ahead will be darker and rougher than you may ever know.
